topic: Namespaces and Friend Functions with Operator Overloading
explanation: In C++, namespaces are used to organize code and prevent name conflicts by encapsulating identifiers within a named scope. Friend functions are non-member functions declared within a class that have access to its private and protected members, enabling controlled external interaction. Operator overloading allows defining custom behaviors for operators (like type conversions or arithmetic) for user-defined types. Combining namespaces, friend functions, and operator overloading enables flexible and encapsulated design of complex types, facilitating clear syntax and extended functionality in modern C++ programming.
